root_cause.text: In the KVM dirty ring handling function `kvm_reset_dirty_gfn()`, an unchecked addition of `offset` and `__fls(mask)` using `u64` arithmetic allows integer wraparound, bypassing the bounds check against `memslot->npages`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a separate check `offset >= memslot->npages` before the addition to ensure the sum cannot wrap, as described in the commit message stating "Range-check offset on its own first, so the addition cannot wrap."

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In the KVM dirty ring handling function `kvm_reset_dirty_gfn()`, an unchecked addition of `offset` and `__fls(mask)` using `u64` arithmetic allows integer wraparound, bypassing the bounds check against `memslot->npages`.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds a separate check `offset >= memslot->npages` before the addition to ensure the sum cannot wrap, as described in the commit message stating "Range-check offset on its own first, so the addition cannot wrap."

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs an unchecked addition of offset and __fls(mask) using u64 arithmetic. When offset is large and __fls(mask) returns a value that causes wraparound, the result becomes smaller than expected, allowing the condition to pass even when the actual address exceeds memslot->npages bounds. This integer overflow vulnerability enables out-of-bounds memory access.
